[AI] Add personal inflation report and dashboard widget
<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request! Make sure to follow the instructions to write release notes for your PR — it should only take a minute or two: https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/#writing-good-release-notes. Try running yarn generate:release-notes *before* pushing your PR for an interactive experience. -->

## Description

<!-- What does this PR do? Why is it needed? Please give context on the "why?": why do we need this change? What problem is it solving for you?-->

<!-- If AI tools wrote a significant part of this change, please disclose it here and name the tool you used. See https://actualbudget.org/docs/contributing/ai-usage-policy -->

This PR adds a new widget and report page to track a user's personal inflation rate. The user can choose a specific window and comparison period for this rate of change. An increase in spending shows a positive percentage in red and a decrease is negative and in green. This feature helps users compare their spending habits over time and see if they want to change their habits to improve their financial situation if, for example, their inflation rate is higher than they would like it to be.
I utilized the Claude Code VSCode extension throughout the implementation of this issue and the git actions to branch, commit, and push my changes.

## Related issue(s)

<!-- e.g. Fixes #123, Relates to #456 -->
Relates to issue #15 

## Testing

<!-- What did you test? How can we reproduce the issue you are fixing or how can we test the feature you built? -->
I used yarn tests and new, Claude-generated, unit tests to ensure the new changes did not break any existing code and they worked how I expected. I also ran the app on my machine with the new feature to manually test it. To try the feature, use the add widget button on the dashboard page to add the "Personal Inflation" widget. 

## Tech Debt

**Introduced:** [Describe any shortcuts, workarounds, or design compromises
made in this implementation, and why. If none, write "None."]
- The per-category monthly spending query in `server/reports/personal-inflation.ts` is a copy of the private `getSumAmountsByMonth` in `server/budget/base.ts`, not a shared helper. A comment points back to the original, but if the budget's filters change, this copy has to be updated by hand or the report will stop matching the budget page.
- The calculation doesn't take rule conditions, so the page has no filter button, unlike most other reports

**Encountered:** [Describe any pre-existing tech debt you ran into while
working on this issue, and how you handled it. If none, write "None."]
- None

<!--- bundlestats-action-comment key:combined end --->
Add Personal Rate of Inflation tracking
**Summary**

Actual Budget already tracks spending by category month over month, but it has no way to surface how much more (or less) a user is spending in a given category relative to a prior period — the personal rate of inflation. Unlike a national CPI figure, a personal inflation rate uses a user's own category weights and actual spending history: if groceries represent 20% of a budget and grocery spending rose 12% year over year, that category contributes differently to the user's real cost-of-living than it would for someone with a 5% grocery weight. A reporting view (and optionally a dashboard widget) that computes month-over-month and year-over-year spending change per category — and an aggregate weighted figure across the full budget — would give users meaningful, personalized inflation visibility that no generic economic index can provide.

**User Story**

As a user who wants to understand my real cost-of-living changes, I want Actual to show me how much my spending in each category has changed versus last month and last year — weighted by each category's share of my total budget — so that I can distinguish genuine price increases from changes in my own habits, without relying on a national inflation figure that doesn't reflect my life.

## User Scenario

A user opens the report and compares their spending by category month over month or year over year. They can see each category's spending change and an aggregate weighted change based on their spending.

## Acceptance Criteria
1. The report shows each category's spending change for month-over-month and year-over-year comparisons.
2. The report shows an aggregate spending change weighted by each category's share of total spending.
3. Categories with insufficient or zero historical spending are handled without calculation errors.
4. The report clearly identifies the periods being compared.

## Out of Scope
- Changing budgets, transactions, or category data.
- Providing a national inflation index.
- Determining whether spending changes are caused by price increases or changes in user behavior.
- Dashboard integration beyond the initial reporting view.

## Open Questions
- Should category weights use budgeted amounts or actual spending?
- Should comparisons use calendar months or rolling periods?
- How should categories with zero or insufficient historical spending affect the aggregate?
- Should this be called "personal inflation" or "spending change"?

**Rough Scope**

Large — The core calculation is straightforward: for each category, compute the percentage change in average monthly spending between two periods, then weight each category by its share of total budgeted or actual spend to produce a composite figure. The data is already present in Actual's database. The complexity lies in the reporting surface: decisions about which periods to compare (calendar month vs. rolling 30 days, prior year same month vs. trailing 12-month average), how to handle categories with zero spend in one period (division-by-zero edge cases), and whether to expose this as a standalone report, an addition to the existing Reports section, or a summary widget on the budget view. A beginner team should start by producing the weighted calculation as a standalone read-only report before attempting any dashboard integration.

**Source**

Requested by a community member in the Actual Budget Discord. Directly analogous to well-established personal-finance analysis (personal CPI / cost-of-living tracking) and a natural extension of Actual's existing category-based reporting. Assisted with Claude for issue generation.
```

1	import * as monthUtils from './months';
2	
3	// Net amount for one category in one month, as stored on transactions
4	// (spending is negative).
5	export type CategoryMonthAmount = {
6	  category: string;
7	  month: string;
8	  amount: number;
9	};
10	
11	// Inclusive range of months, both in `YYYY-MM` format.
12	export type MonthPeriod = {
13	  start: string;
14	  end: string;
15	};
16	
17	export type InflationComparison = 'previous-period' | 'previous-year';
18	
19	export type CategoryInflation = {
20	  category: string;
21	  prior: number;
22	  current: number;
23	  // Share of total prior-period spending, 0-1.
24	  weight: number;
25	  // Fractional change (0.12 = 12% more). `null` when there was no prior
26	  // spending to compare against.
27	  rate: number | null;
28	  // `weight * rate`; the category's share of the overall rate.
29	  contribution: number | null;
30	};
31	
32	export type PersonalInflation = {
33	  current: MonthPeriod;
34	  prior: MonthPeriod;
35	  priorTotal: number;
36	  currentTotal: number;
37	  // Weighted overall change. `null` when there was no prior spending, or
38	  // not enough history to compare against.
39	  rate: number | null;
40	  categories: CategoryInflation[];
41	  // The prior period starts before the first recorded transaction, so its
42	  // spending is incomplete. Rates are left out rather than reported against
43	  // what would look like a drop to zero.
44	  hasInsufficientHistory: boolean;
45	};
46	
47	export type PersonalInflationResult = PersonalInflation & {
48	  // The current period includes a month that hasn't finished yet, so its
49	  // spending is likely understated.
50	  isPartial: boolean;
51	};
52	
53	export function getPeriodLength(period: MonthPeriod) {
54	  return monthUtils.differenceInCalendarMonths(period.end, period.start) + 1;
55	}
56	
57	export function getComparisonPeriod(
58	  period: MonthPeriod,
59	  comparison: InflationComparison,
60	): MonthPeriod {
61	  const offset = comparison === 'previous-year' ? 12 : getPeriodLength(period);
62	  return {
63	    start: monthUtils.subMonths(period.start, offset),
64	    end: monthUtils.subMonths(period.end, offset),
65	  };
66	}
67	
68	// Builds one window of `windowMonths` months ending at each month in
69	// `range`, used to track the rate over time.
70	export function getTrailingPeriods(
71	  range: MonthPeriod,
72	  windowMonths: number,
73	): MonthPeriod[] {
74	  return monthUtils.rangeInclusive(range.start, range.end).map(end => ({
75	    start: monthUtils.subMonths(end, windowMonths - 1),
76	    end,
77	  }));
78	}
79	
80	function sumSpending(
81	  amounts: CategoryMonthAmount[],
82	  categoryIds: Set<string>,
83	  period: MonthPeriod,
84	) {
85	  const totals = new Map<string, number>();
86	  for (const { category, month, amount } of amounts) {
87	    if (
88	      categoryIds.has(category) &&
89	      month >= period.start &&
90	      month <= period.end
91	    ) {
92	      totals.set(category, (totals.get(category) ?? 0) + amount);
93	    }
94	  }
95	
96	  // Flip to positive spending; a category whose refunds outweigh its
97	  // spending counts as no spending rather than negative spending.
98	  const spending = new Map<string, number>();
99	  for (const [category, amount] of totals) {
100	    spending.set(category, Math.max(0, -amount));
101	  }
102	  return spending;
103	}
104	
105	// Personal inflation using the user's own spending as the basket. Each
106	// category's change is weighted by its share of prior-period spending
107	// (base-period weights, as with a Laspeyres index), so a 12% rise in a
108	// category that made up 20% of spending adds 2.4 points to the rate.
109	// Categories with no prior spending have no rate and don't contribute.
110	//
111	// `historyStart` is the first month with any transactions (`null` when
112	// there are none); when given, a prior period that starts earlier is
113	// flagged as having insufficient history.
114	export function calculatePersonalInflation(
115	  amounts: CategoryMonthAmount[],
116	  categoryIds: string[],
117	  current: MonthPeriod,
118	  prior: MonthPeriod,
119	  historyStart?: string | null,
120	): PersonalInflation {
121	  const hasInsufficientHistory =
122	    historyStart === null ||
123	    (historyStart !== undefined && prior.start < historyStart);
124	  const ids = new Set(categoryIds);
125	  const priorSpending = sumSpending(amounts, ids, prior);
126	  const currentSpending = sumSpending(amounts, ids, current);
127	
128	  let priorTotal = 0;
129	  let currentTotal = 0;
130	  for (const id of categoryIds) {
131	    priorTotal += priorSpending.get(id) ?? 0;
132	    currentTotal += currentSpending.get(id) ?? 0;
133	  }
134	
135	  let rate: number | null = null;
136	  const categories: CategoryInflation[] = [];
137	  for (const id of categoryIds) {
138	    const priorAmount = priorSpending.get(id) ?? 0;
139	    const currentAmount = currentSpending.get(id) ?? 0;
140	    if (priorAmount === 0 && currentAmount === 0) {
141	      continue;
142	    }
143	
144	    const weight = priorTotal === 0 ? 0 : priorAmount / priorTotal;
145	    let categoryRate: number | null = null;
146	    let contribution: number | null = null;
147	    if (priorAmount > 0 && !hasInsufficientHistory) {
148	      categoryRate = (currentAmount - priorAmount) / priorAmount;
149	      contribution = weight * categoryRate;
150	      rate = (rate ?? 0) + contribution;
151	    }
152	
153	    categories.push({
154	      category: id,
155	      prior: priorAmount,
156	      current: currentAmount,
157	      weight,
158	      rate: categoryRate,
159	      contribution,
160	    });
161	  }
162	
163	  return {
164	    current,
165	    prior,
166	    priorTotal,
167	    currentTotal,
168	    rate,
169	    categories,
170	    hasInsufficientHistory,
171	  };
172	}
173

22	// Spending per category per month. The filters match the budget's
23	// `sum-amount` cells (see `createCategory` in `server/budget/base.ts`) so
24	// these numbers line up with the spent column on the budget page.
25	async function getCategoryMonthAmounts(
26	  start: string,
27	  end: string,
28	): Promise<CategoryMonthAmount[]> {
29	  const rows = await db.all<{
30	    category: string;
31	    month: number;
32	    amount: number | null;
33	  }>(
34	    `SELECT t.category AS category,
35	            t.date / 100 AS month,
36	            SUM(t.amount) AS amount
37	       FROM v_transactions_internal_alive t
38	       LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account
39	      WHERE t.date >= ? AND t.date <= ?
40	        AND t.category IS NOT NULL
41	        AND a.offbudget = 0
42	      GROUP BY t.category, t.date / 100`,
43	    [monthUtils.bounds(start).start, monthUtils.bounds(end).end],
44	  );
45	
46	  return rows.map(row => {
47	    const month = String(row.month);
48	    return {
49	      category: row.category,
50	      month: `${month.slice(0, 4)}-${month.slice(4)}`,
51	      amount: row.amount ?? 0,
52	    };
53	  });
54	}
55	
56	// The month of the first on-budget transaction, or `null` when there are
57	// none. Months before this have no data, not zero spending.
58	async function getHistoryStart(): Promise<string | null> {
59	  const row = await db.first<{ date: number | null }>(
60	    `SELECT MIN(t.date) AS date
61	       FROM v_transactions_internal_alive t
62	       LEFT JOIN accounts a ON a.id = t.account
63	      WHERE a.offbudget = 0`,
64	  );
65	  if (!row?.date) {
66	    return null;
67	  }
68	  const date = String(row.date);
69	  return `${date.slice(0, 4)}-${date.slice(4, 6)}`;
70	}
71	
72	// Expense categories to include in the basket. Income is never spending;
73	// hidden categories (or ones under a hidden group or parent) are left out
74	// unless asked for.
75	async function getExpenseCategoryIds(includeHidden: boolean) {
76	  const groups = await db.getCategoriesGrouped();
77	  const ids: string[] = [];
78	  for (const group of groups) {
79	    if (group.is_income || (!includeHidden && group.hidden)) {
80	      continue;
81	    }
82	    const hiddenIds = new Set(
83	      group.categories.filter(cat => cat.hidden).map(cat => cat.id),
84	    );
85	    for (const cat of group.categories) {
86	      const isHidden =
87	        hiddenIds.has(cat.id) ||
88	        (cat.parent_id != null && hiddenIds.has(cat.parent_id));
89	      if (!cat.is_income && (includeHidden || !isHidden)) {
90	        ids.push(cat.id);
91	      }
92	    }
93	  }
94	  return ids;
95	}

97	function validatePeriod({ start, end }: MonthPeriod) {
98	  if (
99	    !monthUtils.isValidYearMonth(start) ||
100	    !monthUtils.isValidYearMonth(end)
101	  ) {
102	    throw new ValidationError('Months must be in YYYY-MM format');
103	  }
104	  if (start > end) {
105	    throw new ValidationError('Start month must not be after end month');
106	  }
107	}

110	  return {
111	    ...result,

117	  start,
118	  end,
119	  comparison = 'previous-year',
120	  includeHidden = false,
121	}: MonthPeriod & PersonalInflationOptions): Promise<PersonalInflationResult> {
122	  const current = { start, end };
123	  validatePeriod(current);
124	  const prior = getComparisonPeriod(current, comparison);
125	
126	  const [amounts, categoryIds, historyStart] = await Promise.all([
127	    getCategoryMonthAmounts(prior.start, current.end),
128	    getExpenseCategoryIds(includeHidden),
129	    getHistoryStart(),

132	  return withPartial(

149	  comparison = 'previous-year',

151	}: MonthPeriod &
152	  PersonalInflationOptions & {

16	// How many months of history the trend graph covers
17	export const TREND_MONTHS = 12;
18	
19	export const DEFAULT_COMPARISON: InflationComparison = 'previous-year';

21	// Last calendar year, so the default never includes a partial month
22	export const defaultTimeFrame = {
23	  start: monthUtils.getYearStart(

25	  ),
26	  end: monthUtils.getYearEnd(monthUtils.prevYear(monthUtils.currentMonth())),
27	  mode: 'lastYear',
28	} satisfies TimeFrame;

30	export type PersonalInflationTrendPoint = {
31	  month: string;
32	  date: string;
33	  rate: number | null;
34	  hasInsufficientHistory: boolean;
35	};
36	
37	export type PersonalInflationData = {
38	  // Result for the selected comparison
39	  summary: PersonalInflationResult;
40	  // Results for both comparisons, for showing them side by side
41	  byComparison: Record<InflationComparison, PersonalInflationResult>;
42	  trend: PersonalInflationTrendPoint[];
43	};
44	
45	// One category across both comparisons. An entry is `null` when the
46	// category had no spending in either period of that comparison.
47	export type PersonalInflationCategoryRow = {
48	  category: string;
49	  current: number;
50	  previousPeriod: CategoryInflation | null;
51	  previousYear: CategoryInflation | null;
52	  // The entry for the selected comparison, which share and contribution
53	  // are based on
54	  selected: CategoryInflation | null;
55	};
56	
57	// Some date range presets produce day-shaped bounds; the calculation works
58	// in whole months.
59	export function toMonthPeriod(start: string, end: string): MonthPeriod {
60	  return { start: monthUtils.getMonth(start), end: monthUtils.getMonth(end) };
61	}
62	
63	// Each trend point uses a window the same length as the selected period,
64	// so the final point always matches the headline rate.
65	export function getTrendRange(period: MonthPeriod) {
66	  return {
67	    start: monthUtils.subMonths(period.end, TREND_MONTHS - 1),
68	    end: period.end,
69	    windowMonths: getPeriodLength(period),
70	  };
71	}
72	
73	export function formatPeriod({ start, end }: MonthPeriod, locale: Locale) {
74	  if (start === end) {
75	    return monthUtils.format(start, 'MMMM yyyy', locale);
76	  }
77	  return `${monthUtils.format(start, 'MMM yyyy', locale)} – ${monthUtils.format(end, 'MMM yyyy', locale)}`;
78	}
79	
80	export function formatRate(rate: number, language: string) {
81	  return new Intl.NumberFormat(language, {
82	    style: 'percent',
83	    minimumFractionDigits: 1,
84	    maximumFractionDigits: 1,
85	    signDisplay: 'exceptZero',
86	  }).format(rate);
87	}
88	
89	export function formatShare(share: number, language: string) {
90	  return new Intl.NumberFormat(language, {
91	    style: 'percent',
92	    minimumFractionDigits: 1,
93	    maximumFractionDigits: 1,
94	  }).format(share);
95	}
96	
97	// Joins both comparisons into one row per category, biggest movers in the
98	// selected comparison first. Categories without a contribution (new
99	// spending, or not enough history) go last, largest spending first.
100	export function getCategoryRows(
101	  byComparison: PersonalInflationData['byComparison'],
102	  comparison: InflationComparison,
103	): PersonalInflationCategoryRow[] {
104	  const previousPeriod = new Map(
105	    byComparison['previous-period'].categories.map(c => [c.category, c]),
106	  );
107	  const previousYear = new Map(
108	    byComparison['previous-year'].categories.map(c => [c.category, c]),
109	  );
110	  const ids = new Set([...previousPeriod.keys(), ...previousYear.keys()]);
111	
112	  const rows = [...ids].map(id => {
113	    const row = {
114	      category: id,
115	      current: (previousPeriod.get(id) ?? previousYear.get(id))?.current ?? 0,
116	      previousPeriod: previousPeriod.get(id) ?? null,
117	      previousYear: previousYear.get(id) ?? null,
118	    };
119	    return {
120	      ...row,
121	      selected:
122	        comparison === 'previous-period'
123	          ? row.previousPeriod
124	          : row.previousYear,
125	    };
126	  });
127	
128	  return rows.sort((a, b) => {
129	    const aContribution = a.selected?.contribution ?? null;
130	    const bContribution = b.selected?.contribution ?? null;
131	    if (aContribution === null || bContribution === null) {
132	      if (aContribution !== bContribution) {
133	        return aContribution === null ? 1 : -1;
134	      }
135	      return b.current - a.current;
136	    }
137	    return Math.abs(bContribution) - Math.abs(aContribution);
138	  });
139	}
140

143	  if (rate === null) {
144	    return theme.pageTextSubdued;
145	  }
146	  if (rate === 0) {
147	    return theme.tableText;
148	  }
149	  return rate > 0 ? theme.reportsNumberNegative : theme.reportsNumberPositive;
150	}

171	        comparison: 'previous-period',
172	      }),
173	      send('reports/personal-inflation', {
174	        ...period,
175	        comparison: 'previous-year',
176	      }),
177	      send('reports/personal-inflation-series', {
178	        ...getTrendRange(period),
179	        comparison,
180	      }),
181	    ]);
182	
183	    setData({
184	      summary: comparison === 'previous-period' ? previousPeriod : previousYear,
185	      byComparison: {
186	        'previous-period': previousPeriod,
187	        'previous-year': previousYear,
188	      },
189	      trend: series.map(point => ({
190	        month: point.current.end,
191	        date: monthUtils.format(point.current.end, "MMM ''yy", locale),
192	        rate: point.rate,
193	        hasInsufficientHistory: point.hasInsufficientHistory,
194	      })),

196	  };

+---
+category: Features
+authors: [RaccoonSwarm]
+---
+
+Add Personal Inflation report and dashboard widget showing how your spending has changed across categories
# Issue #15 -- Add Personal Rate of Inflation tracking

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](15-raccoonswarm-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](15-raccoonswarm-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

   The two most central classes are `shared/personal-inflation.ts` and `server/budget/base.ts`. The new `shared/personal-inflation.ts` calculates the personal inflation rate: it weights each category's spending change by that category's share of prior-period spending, and handles categories with no history without dividing by zero. The existing `server/budget/base.ts` is where Actual already totals spending per category each month. My server code uses the same query filters, so the report's numbers match the Budget page.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

   The most significant relationship is the dependency from `server/reports/personal-inflation.ts` to `shared/personal-inflation.ts`, labeled "calls calculatePersonalInflation()". It shows how the solution splits its work: the server module gets the data (monthly spending, expense categories and where the budget's history starts) from the database, then passes it to the shared module, which does only the math. This matters because it keeps the calculation separate from the database, so it can be tested on its own, and the same logic serves both the single report and the 12-month trend.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

   I would change how `server/reports/personal-inflation.ts` gets its spending data. Right now it copies the query filters from `getSumAmountsByMonth` in `server/budget/base.ts` instead of sharing them, so if the budget's filters ever change, the report could stop matching the Budget page without anyone noticing. I would move that query into a shared helper that both modules use. I would also combine the three separate requests the report makes into one, since each currently reloads the same categories and history from the database.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

   The sequence starts when the user opens the Personal Inflation report, or changes its date range or comparison (for example, picking "Last month" and "Compare to previous period"). When it completes successfully, the report shows the overall personal inflation rate, the two periods being compared, a 12-month trend graph, and a table of each category's change against both the previous period and the same months last year.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

   The first important step is the three parallel `send()` calls from `personal-inflation-spreadsheet` (new code), which request the previous-period comparison, the same-months-last-year comparison, and the trend at the same time so the table can show both comparisons side by side; they travel through the existing `send()` connection to `ReportsHandlers` (modified). The second is the server module `server/reports/personal-inflation.ts` (new code) querying the existing SQLite database for monthly spending per category, the expense categories, and the month of the first transaction, using the same filters as the budget's existing spent totals. The third is the call to `calculatePersonalInflation` in `shared/personal-inflation.ts` (new code), which weights each category's change by its share of prior spending, adds up the overall rate, and returns null rates when there isn't enough history.

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

   The diagram leaves out invalid date ranges, which the server rejects in `validatePeriod`, and a request failing, in which case the report stays on its loading indicator. It also leaves out the alternative results: comparisons with insufficient history, new categories with no prior spending, periods that include the unfinished current month, and saving the settings to the dashboard widget. I left these out to keep the diagram focused on the main success path. The alternative results don't add new steps, since they come back as flags and null values from the same calculation, and saving the widget uses existing dashboard code.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

   I used AI (Claude Code) to create both diagrams as Mermaid code, including the color coding for new, modified, and existing code and the annotation notes, based on the code it helped me write for this issue. I reviewed the rendered images and checked the classes, methods, and steps against the actual files in my branch. Corrections included fixing colors and notes that didn't render and enlarging boxes whose text didn't fit. I also narrowed the deliverable to the server/data class diagram and the sequence diagram.

I didn't run the e2e/VRT tests. All four acceptance criteria in #15 are met, and nothing blocks a merge.

| Criterion | Score (1–10) | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Correctness — does the change do what the issue asked? | **9** | **Meets all four ACs.**<br>1. The category table shows previous-period and previous-year changes side by side.<br>2. The headline rate weights each category by its share of prior-period spending.<br>3. Categories with no prior spending get a `null` rate instead of dividing by zero, and comparisons that start before the budget's first transaction show "Insufficient history".<br>4. Each view states the two periods being compared, e.g. "Jan–Dec 2025 compared with Jan–Dec 2024".<br><br>**Small UX edge case:** the "Spent X before, Y now" totals include categories that are new this period, but the rate leaves them out. If all extra spending is in a new category, the rate can read 0.0% while the totals clearly went up. The explainer text covers this, but it may still confuse users. |
| Test coverage — are tests present and meaningful? | **9** | **Strong coverage:**<br>- 17 tests for the calculation (weights, refunds, zero/new categories, insufficient history, period math)<br>- 11 server tests against a real DB (off-budget, hidden and income filtering, validation)<br>- 8 tests for the spreadsheet helpers<br>- E2E/VRT screenshots for the report and widget<br><br>**Gap:** the React components (`PersonalInflationCategoryTable`, `PersonalInflationCard`) have no unit tests, though the VRTs partly cover them. |
| Code quality — consistent style, clear naming, no unnecessary duplication | **9** | Clean split: the math in `shared/` is pure, `server/` only fetches data, and the UI follows the existing report and card patterns. The duplicated budget query is acknowledged in the Tech Debt section. Minor inefficiency: the card makes all three server calls even though it shows only one comparison, and each call reloads categories and history. |
| Documentation — inline comments and PR description are clear | **10** | Comments explain the reasoning, such as the Laspeyres weighting and why refunds are clamped. The PR description is complete and includes an honest Tech Debt section. The release note follows repo conventions. The report page explains the calculation to users. |
| AI transparency — if AI was used, is there evidence of human verification? | **9** | The PR names Claude Code, commits are prefixed `[AI]` with co-author trailers, and the diagram Q&A describes checking against the code and fixing errors. No AI session logs are committed on the branch. |
| **Overall — would you merge this as-is?** | **9** | **Yes.** The totals-vs-rate wording and the missing component tests are optional follow-ups. |
